independence_declaration.statement:
I am code-security-reviewer, session a087192e (task T-DG7-REV-CS-R5). I verified the assignment's sha256, e7b188dd…951a. I authored no implementation in the DG7 scope.

- P7 is by solution-architect, backend-workflow-engineer, kpi-benefits-engineer, frontend-ux-engineer, transformation-analyst and devops-engineer (docs/delivery/handbacks/DG7/).
- The acceptance suites are by qa-verifier.
- The freeze, the stages.json repair (9d5691143), D-277, the drills and the pre-freeze checks are by the delivery-orchestrator.

I formed this verdict before reading any other round-5 record. My private staging view does not contain the other reviewers' round-5 records, and I opened none of them. The domain reviewer's run was auto-committed (7b7bbfbdd) while I was working; I saw only its file names in a `git diff --stat`.

At the start, HEAD was f3f61cd60 ('DG7: freeze round 5'), the direct child of the source commit 02aeed6e4. The freeze commit adds only gate metadata (three assignments, the candidate manifest and stages.json), all excluded from the manifest. The candidate ID recomputes to 07af9fba…a61d on the working tree, with --ref 02aeed6e4, and on a full disposable clone checked out at 02aeed6e4 (3155 files). --diff matches.

Record-format note: the assignment says 'round: 7', but its own title, task id and record path say round 5. tools/gates/lib/rules.mjs:682 and :794 reject a record whose round differs from its round-N directory. I therefore record round 5. The assignment's mirror template docs/delivery/reviews/DG5/round-5/code-security-reviewer.json does not exist (DG5/round-5 holds only release-auditor.json), so I mirrored my DG7 round-4 record, which conforms to review.schema.json.

List every git change between the round-4 source commit (471072d64) and the round-5 source commit (02aeed6e4).

Round-5 records are listed as 'missing' because they are being written in this round. --pipeline: 'PASS pipeline (active stage: DG7 REVIEWING)', exit 0.
--pipeline ran twice. Run A, in the validator loop, exited 0 with PASS. Mid-run its log looked empty and `ps` in the nested sandbox did not show the process, so I started run B (8m50s), which also exited 0 with PASS. Both wrote the same file, as 41-validators-pipeline.log explains.

The release-auditor writes that record after the three reviews, so it cannot exist during REVIEWING. The round-4 failure 'stages.json: DG7 illegal transition REVIEWING -> REVIEWING' (round-4/40-validators.log, 41-validators-pipeline.log) appears in none of these runs. The overall exit_status of this check is 0 because every mode that can pass during REVIEWING passed.

checks_run.procedure:
Independent probe of the stages.json repair (9d5691143), with three parts.
P1, on DG7's history: transitions; time order; each REVIEWING entry aligned with its round's frozen_at; exactly one FIXING entry between consecutive rounds, strictly inside the interval; the current candidate equal to round 5. Other stages are scanned for time order (INFO only).
P2: the late entry's timestamp checked against git history. Also: does the repair change or remove any pre-existing DG7 history entry (round-4 freeze a76c2aed4 vs 9d5691143)?
P3, mutation in a disposable --shared clone at 02aeed6e4: run --historical --stage DG6 as a control, then again after removing the late entry. The validator must fail again with the round-4 error.
checks_run.environment: Live repository read-only, plus a disposable --shared clone under $TMPDIR (removed afterwards). Node 24.21.0.
checks_run.expected: P1: DG7 is REVIEWING -> FIXING -> REVIEWING for each of the 4 completed rounds and time-monotone. P2: exactly one entry marked 'recorded late', with a truthful timestamp; no existing entry altered. P3: control exit 0; mutant exit 1 with 'illegal transition REVIEWING -> REVIEWING'.
checks_run.actual:
Run 2 (10-history-probe.log): exit 0.
P1 PASS. DG7: PLANNED -> BUILDING -> REVIEWING(r1) -> FIXING -> REVIEWING(r2) -> FIXING -> REVIEWING(r3) -> FIXING@2026-11-16T01:38:50Z (the late entry) -> REVIEWING(r4)@03:55:37Z -> FIXING@06:12:55Z -> REVIEWING(r5)@06:14:07Z. The history is time-monotone. Each completed round is followed by exactly one FIXING strictly inside the interval. Rounds 3–5 REVIEWING entries equal frozen_at. Rounds 1 and 2 are 22 s and 18 s after frozen_at; these are pre-existing entries written by those freeze commits, unchanged since round 2, and the validator does not require equality. stage = REVIEWING = last entry, and the candidate equals round 5.
INFO: DG0 [56]REVIEWING@2026-09-30T15:45Z > [57]FIXING@15:16Z and DG5 [5]VERIFYING@2026-10-26T12:00Z > [6]APPROVED@06:30Z are not time-monotone. Both are pre-existing in approved gates and identical at 471072d64 and a76c2aed4, so they predate this round. The validator does not check time order, and its historical runs for DG5 and DG1 pass. This is an observation outside this round's change, not a finding.
P2 PASS. Exactly one entry is marked 'recorded late'. Its at, 2026-11-16T01:38:50Z, equals the commit time of 5458273cd 'DG7: import round-3 findings; assignments AN-P7G and BE-R8', as the note states. The repair commits AN-P7G (c3e2a77b8, 01:59:30Z) and BE-R8 (449d66004, 02:23:44Z) fall inside the inserted FIXING -> REVIEWING(r4) window, so the entry records what really happened. Comparing 9d5691143 with the round-4 freeze a76c2aed4: 0 entries removed or changed, 2 added (the late round-3 FIXING and the round-4 FIXING), and the pre-existing order is kept.
P3 PASS. Control: --historical --stage DG6 exit 0, PASS. Mutant (late entry removed): exit 1, 'stages.json: DG7 illegal transition REVIEWING -> REVIEWING', which is exactly the round-4 defect. The validator still catches this class, and the inserted entry is what makes it pass.
Run 1 (10-history-probe-run1.log), exit 1, has two causes, both mine:
(a) P1 used invariants stricter than the validator over all stages and counted the DG0/DG5 INFO items and the round-1/2 offsets as failures.
(b) P3 hit 'No space left on device' while cloning, because my earlier 6.4 GB full clone had filled the shared scratch disk. The subsequent ENOENT/'Cannot find module' errors follow from the failed clone.
I deleted that clone and rewrote the probe as v2 (strict on DG7 only; --shared clone). P2 already passed in run 1.
Judgement: a late-recorded entry is an acceptable repair. Its timestamp is the real outcome time, not the repair time. It is disclosed in its own note and in D-277. It alters no existing entry. It is the only repair that both makes the history truthful and satisfies the state machine (appending a new FIXING could not remove the REVIEWING -> REVIEWING pair). It is the same repair that closed F-DG4-104/124 (DG4 history: 'FIXING@2026-10-13T10:52 [late]') and F-DG6-911/951 ('FIXING@2026-11-11T06:42:33 [late]') in gates now APPROVED.
Observation, not a finding: this is the fourth occurrence of this process error. D-277 says the freeze step 'now checks' for transition errors. No tooling change implements that check (tools/gates is unchanged), so it is a process commitment I cannot verify mechanically. The validator still fails closed on it, and the round-5 freeze itself is correct.

summary:
Verdict PASS on candidate sha256:07af9fba…a61d (source 02aeed6e4; freeze f3f61cd60). F-DG7-941 (mine) and the identical F-DG7-922 and F-DG7-970 are CLOSED_VERIFIED. stages.json now records REVIEWING -> FIXING -> REVIEWING for every DG7 round. --historical DG6…DG1, --reconcile and --pipeline exit 0. --stage DG7 fails only on the gate record, which the auditor has not written yet.
The late-recorded round-3 FIXING entry is an acceptable repair. Its timestamp equals the round-3 findings import (5458273cd, 01:38:50Z), and it is disclosed in its note and in D-277. No existing entry is changed. Removing it brings back the exact round-4 validator failure. It matches the accepted DG4 and DG6 precedents.
Since round 4, the only change to the manifest is the D-277 row; no product, test, handover or tooling file changed. secret-scan (payload and history), claims-scan, check-handover (default and strict) and 192 security tool tests pass. My round-4 product review carries forward, with every failure line in its logs explained.
No new findings. Observations (not defects): pre-existing non-monotone timestamps in the approved DG0 and DG5 histories; and D-277's 'freeze step now checks' is a process commitment with no tooling change, though the validator still fails closed. Record round set to 5, not the assignment's 'round: 7', because rules.mjs requires it to match round-5/.
